questions.question: Give three positive effects of trade unions on a business and explain each.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, explained: one organised partner to negotiate with, so agreements cover all workers for a fixed period and wage costs are predictable; orderly grievance and dispute procedures, so problems are solved early before they cause stoppages; better morale and lower labour turnover, saving recruitment and training costs; safer working conditions, so fewer lost days and claims; support for skills development through SETAs, raising productivity; a channel of communication for introducing change.

questions.question: A business has 40 workers earning R8 000 a month. Calculate the monthly cost of a 6 percent increase, and the output lost in a 10-day strike if daily output is worth R60 000.
questions.expected_answer: Each worker: 8 000 x 6 / 100 = R480 more a month. For 40 workers: 40 x 480 = R19 200 a month (R230 400 a year). Strike: 60 000 x 10 = R600 000 of output lost.

questions.question: Explain how trade unions can contribute to sustainable economic growth, and one way they can hinder it.
questions.expected_answer: Contribute: fair wages share the benefits of growth and increase spending; training raises skills and productivity; social dialogue at NEDLAC creates stability that encourages investment; health and safety and decent work; support for a just transition to cleaner energy. Hinder: long or violent strikes discourage investment, or wage increases far above productivity reduce employment and competitiveness.
